comments.note: src/cli.ts hard-codes VERSION = '0.1.0' as a string constant rather than importing it from package.json. For a release-managed library, VERSION should either be imported from package.json (with resolveJsonModule enabled) or derived from the build-time __PKG_VERSION__ injection that tsup supports — this keeps it in sync automatically. Not blocking for 0.1.0 but worth addressing before 1.0.

The onSuccess script in tsup.config.ts that chmods dist/cli.js uses inline CJS node -e code and calls /bin/sh: node which is absent in some CI environments (as evidenced by exit code 127 during build). A more robust approach is to run chmod via an explicit postbuild npm script or use tsup's built-in banner option to ensure executable permissions are set correctly across platforms. Pre-existing issue, not introduced by WP-007.

The integration test file (tests/integration/build.test.ts) was placed in tests/integration/ which is not explicitly mentioned in the vitest.config.ts include pattern (tests/**/*.test.{js,ts}) — but tests/**/ does cover it. The test directory itself required mkdir. Consider documenting the tests/ sub-directory structure in a tests/README or a comment in vitest.config.ts for contributor clarity.

The default Claude Code frontmatter template in src/builders/frontmatter.ts references {{cc_model}}, {{cc_permission_mode}}, and {{cc_memory}}, but none of these fields are validated or documented as required in SuiteConfig or BuildConfig. The fixture was missing cc_model (fixed in this WP). A built-in validator or at least a documented list of 'expected context variables per target' would prevent silent {{unresolved}} markers in user output.

comments.note: check mode with a plugin reporting errors: summary.success remains true and strictFailures stays empty when check=true but strict=false. This is correct behaviour for the AC ('exits 1 when validators report errors') only applies when --check is used alongside --strict or when the build() caller checks the result manually. The AC wording is slightly ambiguous — the CLI exits 1 only in strict mode, not in plain check mode. No fix needed for 0.1.0 but the AC and CLI help text could be aligned more precisely.

VERSION is duplicated: hard-coded in src/cli.ts as '0.1.0' AND exported as a const from src/index.ts. Both are '0.1.0' today but they will drift on future bumps unless the release process updates both. Developer's own comment flags this. Consider consolidating to a single source before 1.0.

No test covers CLI invocation as a child process (exec dist/cli.js and assert exit code). The integration test covers build() programmatically and the manual verification confirms the CLI, but an automated end-to-end child-process test (spawn + exit code assertion) would give stronger regression protection for the CLI layer. Nice-to-have for a future QA pass.

summary: Reviewed all four Developer-modified files: src/cli.ts, tests/integration/build.test.ts, README.md, fixtures/sample-suite/meta/_shared.yaml.
No blocking issues found. All six acceptance criteria are structurally sound and architecturally appropriate.
Two Fix-Forward changes applied directly (non-behavioral, QA results remain valid):

1. VERSION sourced from package.json in both src/cli.ts and src/index.ts — eliminates the dual hard-coded '0.1.0' constant flagged by both Developer and QA. tsconfig.json already had resolveJsonModule: true; createRequire (already imported in cli.ts) is reused for both callsites. Zero behavior change.

2. Corrected misleading --check help text in both the file-level JSDoc comment and the USAGE string constant. The old text claimed '--check exits 1 when validators report errors', which was incorrect — plain --check always exits 0; exit 1 only occurs when --strict is also set. Clarified both locations to accurately describe the combined --check --strict semantics.
Documentation-forward items tagged for Documentation agent (see comments).

One code-smell noted: TargetType is re-exported from both builders/index.ts and plugins/index.ts, both of which flow into src/index.ts via export *. TypeScript accepts duplicate type-only re-exports without error (confirmed by QA's noEmit pass), but the redundancy is worth cleaning up before 1.0.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied: VERSION in src/cli.ts changed from hardcoded '0.1.0' string constant to `createRequire(import.meta.url)('../package.json').version`. Reuses the existing createRequire import already present in the file. Non-behavioral — USAGE string and --version output remain identical at 0.1.0.

Fix-Forward applied: VERSION in src/index.ts changed from `export const VERSION = '0.1.0'` to reading package.json via createRequire. Eliminates the dual hard-coded string that Developer and QA both flagged as a drift risk on future bumps. Non-behavioral.

Fix-Forward applied: Corrected misleading --check exit-code semantics in two locations within src/cli.ts: (1) the file-header JSDoc comment block, and (2) the USAGE string constant. Previous text 'Exits 1 when validators report errors' was factually wrong for plain --check (exit 1 only triggers in strict mode). Updated both to accurately state that --check alone always exits 0 and that --strict must be combined to get exit 1 on validation failures. Non-behavioral — no code logic changed.

TargetType is re-exported from both src/plugins/index.ts and src/builders/index.ts, both flowing into src/index.ts via `export *`. TypeScript silently accepts duplicate type-only re-exports, but this is confusing — a future contributor adding a value export with the same name from both paths would get a hard error. The canonical home for TargetType is plugins/types.ts; builders/index.ts should not re-export it and the duplicate in builders/types.ts (`export type { TargetType } from '../plugins/types.js'`) should be dropped. Low impact for 0.1.0 — address before 1.0.

[documentation-forward] The default Claude Code frontmatter template (DEFAULT_FRONTMATTER_CLAUDE_CODE in src/builders/frontmatter.ts) references {{cc_model}}, {{cc_permission_mode}}, and {{cc_memory}}, but none of these are listed in the BuildConfig reference or SuiteConfig table in README.md as required YAML fields. Add a note under the 'Default frontmatter templates' section (or in a new 'Required YAML fields per target' subsection) documenting which metadata fields the default templates expect, so users know what to include in their _shared.yaml or per-persona YAML files.

[documentation-forward] The tests/ sub-directory structure (engine/, builders/, loaders/, plugins/, validators/, integration/) is undocumented. Add either a brief tests/README.md or inline comments in vitest.config.ts explaining the test directory layout so contributors know where to add new tests.

[documentation-forward] The exported VERSION constant from src/index.ts is undocumented in the public API surface. It should either be mentioned in the README under a 'Exports' or 'API' section, or (if intentionally semi-private) marked with @internal in its JSDoc. Currently the JSDoc comment is minimal.
